customer_acme: Hey team — during a live demo just now our tenant acme-prod-01 went from ~full credits to 0 and the API started returning 429s mid-session. Demo interrupted, not sure what triggered it.

sam (support): Sorry about that. Can you paste the exact wall time (UTC) and one X-Request-Id from the failing requests? Also were you on Hosted or Dedicated?

customer_acme: Timestamp ~2026-03-17T15:07:12Z. Example header: X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d. We're on Hosted. Multiple users streaming during the demo, several parallel sessions (~6). UI showed full credits until about 15s before the 429s started.

kevin (eng): Thanks. Two quick questions: 1) Were you using long-lived streaming connections or short requests? 2) Any client-side caching of the quota shown in the UI?

customer_acme: Long-lived streaming for the chat window. The demo app keeps a cached quota value but also polls /usage occasionally. It didn't poll between the start of the demo and the 429s.

ingrid (billing): No plan changes on our side? No promo or upgrade that could have caused recalc?

customer_acme: Nothing changed. Same plan for months. No promo.

rate_limit_bot: Alert: burst window exceeded for tenant acme-prod-01 — 5,240 tokens in 60s (threshold 5,000). First observed 2026-03-17T15:06:58Z.

sam (support): That alert is helpful. Sounds like a burst exceeded the short-window quota and server started issuing soft 429s. Two important possibilities: 1) streaming + concurrency can spike short-window token accounting, and 2) there's a known edge where background top-up and UI cache invalidation race under heavy retries.

kevin (eng): Agreed. On Hosted we have a top-up job that reconciles usage and credits at minute boundaries. If many concurrent sessions drain tokens and client retries happen, the top-up can lag visible state by ~30–90s in edge load. We should check the backend correlation for req_0a1b2c3d and the quota-service logs around 15:06:50–15:07:30Z.

sam (support): Can you try this quick repro curl (from the demo environment) and paste the output?

```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "X-Demo-Context: acme-demo" \
  -d '{"model":"openllm-small","prompt":"test","max_tokens":1024}'
```

We want headers X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-Request-Id.

customer_acme: Running now — got 429, headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 30, X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d. UI still showed 2187 tokens for a moment earlier.

kevin (eng): That matches the race theory: UI cache (client-side) showed stale positive balance while backend had already depleted the short-window bucket and enforced 429s. For demos, shorter streaming segments or explicit per-request budget checks help.

sam (support): Short-term workaround: restart long-lived streams or rotate the API key for the demo session — that forces a fresh quota view. Also implement a quick client check against the /quota endpoint before starting a large streaming demo. Example: `GET /v1/quota?tenant=acme-prod-01` returns authoritative tokens.

ingrid (billing): For clarification — monthly bucket full refills occur at your tenant anchor time (billing anchor) processed in UTC at 00:00 plus backend reconciliation. In heavy load we sometimes see the UI surface the new value earlier due to CDN/cache invalidation, but the authoritative refill is the quota service record. If you saw the UI jump earlier, that can be misleading.

customer_acme: Ok makes sense. For future demos we need a checklist — avoid high-concurrency streaming and check /quota first. Anything else you recommend?

kevin (eng): We'll also add a note in the docs about streaming demos and short-window burst accounting. I opened an internal ticket to look at reducing the reconciliation lag under heavy retry storms.

sam (support): I'll escalate to infra with the request-id and the burst alert. Can you DM me the full logs if possible? We'll include timings and session ids in the escalation.

customer_acme: DMing logs now. Thanks — appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup:

sam (support): No problem. We'll follow up with a postmortem if we confirm a top-up race. In the meantime, use the /quota check and lower concurrent stream count for demos.
